title: bug: sh and ps1 wrappers record different ref forms for branch landings
description: record_commit for a committed completion/checkpoint gets ref=<branch> from moe-agent.sh (LAND_BRANCH, e.g. moe/work-2026-10-29) but ref=refs/heads/<branch> from moe-agent.ps1 (Invoke-MoeLanding, 3 call sites). The daemon stores it as reported, so task.commits / landing metadata differ by wrapper. Repro: postflight-owner-guard.cjs sequential case on ps1 (ledger completion row ref). Pick one form for both wrappers and add a parity assertion.
definitionOfDone: Both wrappers send the same ref form for branch landings (completion and checkpoint, including the post-CAS resend paths)
A postflight harness case asserts the exact ref on both sh and ps1

implementationPlan.description:
WRAPPER FIX: every committed branch-landing row sends the bare branch name. Anchors are identical at HEAD and in the merge 3f6817f1.
- scripts/moe-agent.ps1, Invoke-MoeLanding: the three record_commit rows of a committed landing, all on the `$branch` the CAS just moved.
  1. The normal row: `$recArgs = @{ ... ref = "refs/heads/$branch"` → `ref = $branch`.
  2. The catch block's post-CAS row: `Send-MoeRecordCommit @{taskId=$TaskId;outcome='committed';kind=$Kind;sha=$new;ref="refs/heads/$branch";` → `ref=$branch;`.
  3. The finally block's post-CAS resend, under `if ($casOk -and -not $recorded)`: `...sha=$res.Sha;ref="refs/heads/$branch";` → `ref=$branch;`.
  - Leave every other `refs/heads/$branch` alone: the rev-parse check, the journal `target`, the CAS update-ref, and both `$res.Ref` assignments. `$res.Ref` is internal: rescue routing and the outcome classification read it, and it is never sent for a committed row.
  - Leave the rescue rows (`ref = $res.Ref`, Invoke-MoeRescueRef's `$ref`) alone.
- Owed-ledger replay, both wrappers. This crash path re-sends a lost committed completion row from the receipt journal. The journal keeps `target` = refs/heads/<branch>: it is the delivery receipt's target and the replay's rev-parse input. Only the row's ref drops the prefix, and only when something remains after it (case-sensitive, like git refs).
  - ps1 Send-MoeOwedLedgerRow, replacing `ref=[string]$Journal.target`:
    $t=[string]$Journal.target; $p='refs/heads/'; $ownedRef = if ($t.StartsWith($p, [StringComparison]::Ordinal) -and $t.Length -gt $p.Length) { $t.Substring($p.Length) } else { $t }
    then use `ref=$ownedRef`.
  - sh receipt_ledger_send, in the python heredoc, replacing `ref=d['target']`:
    t=d['target']; p='refs/heads/'; ref=t[len(p):] if t.startswith(p) and len(t)>len(p) else t
    Use slicing, not str.removeprefix: older macOS python3 lacks it.
  - Keep both log lines naming the full target.
- Error handling is unchanged. The rows stay best-effort: Send-MoeRecordCommit and record_commit_rpc never break the loop. An owed row still leaves its journal only when the daemon acknowledges it. A non-empty ref is guaranteed, so the daemon's missingRequired('ref') can never refuse the replay.
- Checks:
  - `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`;
  - `head -c3 scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | od -An -tx1` prints ef bb bf (UTF-8 with BOM, which parity-check enforces);
  - `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` passes.
  - Step 3's postflight.ps1 run parses and executes the ps1, so a ps1 syntax error fails it.
Use the Edit tool. Report scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 in complete_step.modifiedFiles.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Full refs/heads/<branch> everywhere. Rejected: it contradicts the documented record_commit contract (docs/MCP_SERVER.md says 'branch name') and the daemon's own tool description. It would also need edits to sh's normal and teardown paths plus the docs. (2) Normalize in the daemon by stripping on store. Rejected as scope: the DoD asks for wrapper parity, the daemon stores ref as reported by design, and the change would need daemon tests and a rebuild. (3) Change $res.Ref too. Rejected: it is internal, rescue routing reads it, and it is never sent for a committed row. (4) Leave the owed-ledger replay on the full target. Rejected: the replay re-sends a committed row lost after the CAS, so it would bring back the mixed form that the DoD's resend clause forbids. And since the daemon merges rows by sha+kind, a replay in a different form could flip the stored ref. (5) Align the non-committed rows too: sh's nothing/refused/failed rows carry the branch, while ps1's carry none or a rescue ref. Not needed: the daemon ignores ref unless outcome is committed, and lastCommitOutcome stores no ref.

- WSLENV on this box shares only TERMINAL_EMULATOR and TERM_SESSION_ID, so MOE_* variables reach Windows processes only when added to WSLENV.
